PREFACE TO THE SIXTH EDITION
Tt gives me great pleasure to present the sixth
revised enlarged edition ol this book which, judging
from the sales and letlers received by ine, is serving
a useful purpose among the intelligentsia, 1 have
taken this opportunity to rewrite cerlam passages,
rearrange some sections, add to vilal information
and generally bring it up-to-date.
In these additions and allerations [ have been
guided by the solitary principle of increasing ils
utilitarian value. For instance, I have given practical
methods of predicting price movements of bullion,
cotton and share values of popular scrips, In the latter
case I have disclosed a treasure by giving the sensitive
points which, as I found, react to price fluctuations
of important industrials, Two new chapters, one
on the mighty sub-planet Mandi and the other on
daily guide have been added. An unfailing method
of measuring longevily (6nd of Man) has been outlined
and the chapter on judgment of horoscopes has been
further amplified and streamlined in the light of new
experience. I have reduced mathematical work in
the erection of horoscopes and dasa calculations (o
the minimum by the introduction of new Tables which
will make the work infinitely easy. By way of sample
studies I have given the horoscopes of top-rank Indian
leaders, Marshal Stalin and Independent India whieh
will be found to be of greal interest lo readers,
That the book has created an abiding interest in
the subject of astrology among intelligent people,
there is no shadow of doubt, for numerous corres
pondents have pressed me to write a larger hook on
Indian astrology incorporating advanced methods
of prediction, I may inform them that I have accepted
their mandate and the work is on hand. Let us hopr
it will not be Jong before it is, published. js:

In the course of his long experience in the science of
astrology, extending to two decades, the author has
found that the Indian as well as the Western system.
of astrology are essentially one and the same, Tf ene
has the merit of an ancient and glorious heritage,
the other can boast of an uncanny precision in the
matter of calculation of planetary and other positions
which is perhaps the sive gua non of correct predic
tion. Efficiency rather than expediency dictates that
the best of both the systems should be capitalized.
Tn the pages that follow, therefore, the author has
tried to explain the working of both the systems in as
compact and practical a manner as possible.
While he has taken care to differentiate between
the two systems in the text itself, the author wishes
fo stress the fact that the student should stick to one
method at-a time. He must not, for inslance, cast the
horoscope by one method and interpret it by another,

EVERYDAY ASTROLOGY
CHAPTER I
THE TWO SYSTEMS
Astronomy is the science that deals with the
physical phenomena of heavenly bodlics, their consti-
tution, motion, attraction and the resultant manifes-
tations which are porccptible to the physical eye. The
eclipse, the new moon, and the full moon are illus-
trations in point.
Astrology however treats aboul the influence of
those heavenly bodies—we mean the planets and the
stars—on human life and affairs connected with it,
It is a science in the sense that ils whole edifice is
built on scientific data. It is an art in the sonse that
man interprets the influence of these bodies on life.
It is a much debated queslion whether the stars
have any influence at all on human life, While we
do not propose to concern ourselves with that contro-
vetsy here, we may bo permitted to express our opinion
that, judging from recorded facts and our own oxpe-
rience, we are forced to the conclusion that the hea-
venly bodies do exert a considerable influence on life in
this world. Not only thai, they give us an inkling as to
the nature of our past as well as fulure. It is the busi-
ness of us mortals to be guided by such indications
towards a better adjustment of our lives.

3x8 EVERYDAY ASLROLOGY
The Sun, Jupiter and Venus are strong during
daytime, while the Moon, Mars and Saturn are strong
during night. Mercury is strong both at night and
during day. Benefics are strong during the Moon’s
waxing period and the malcfics are strong dming the
waning period.
Really speaking the strength of planets is cal-
culated by quite a number of means, all of course
depending originally upon their longitudes, The most
important among them are called vargas. They are:
hora, dreshkana, navamsa, dwadasamsa, thrimsamsa,
etc. All of them involve division of the house into
2, 3, 9, I, 30 etc. parts and the finding of the tah ead
position in those divisions.for which particular effects
are predicted. In view of the fact that our time of
birth in a majoroiFt caysé s happens to be rough, iti s
impossible to rely on the above effects. In actual
practice therefore we recommend only (1) hora,
(2)_dreshkana and (3) vavamsa. Planets occupying
good places according to the above divisions may be
said to be strong.
Planets are strong when receiving benefic aspects
from other powerful planets, adverse rays not affecting.
Planets are weak when occupying hoyses of debili-
tation (neccha), enemy houses, or 67 8, 12° But if
these happen to be uehcha, own or friends’ or houses of

rior. :

Month of Katak (July 20 to Aug. 19 approx.) :
This is an unfortunate position; for, persons born
in this month are not rich asarule. To make matters
worse, they have an independent nature which makes
them, if only out of pique, disregard well-meant
advice; and they have a very sharp intellect.
Another unfortunate aspect of the whole thing is
that they will have to work for others and never
perhaps for their own, They will also for the most
part be itinerant in their career. Sorrowfulness will
cloud their life.
Month of Simha (Aug. 20 10 Sept. 19 approx.) :
Those born during this month will be great lovers of
nature. They will try to spend all their lives, if they
can, in jungles and mountains. Sometimes that
love devolves on sheep and poultry. They have a
strong constitution and keep robust health, If the
$un is strong, they will bo great scholars and attain
mastery over the sciences and arts. They have an
inherent organising ability which should greatly help
them in their lives, :
* Month of Kanya (Spt. 20 to Oct. 19 approx.) :
Children of ‘this month will be great intellectttals,
They will be men of letters, musicians, artists,
mathematicians, astrologers, poets; etc. They will
be wordly to the core with an uncanny knowledge of
the ways of men and things. They will be feminine
in their personality and of delicate constitution. They
Are likely to be a bit shy in’ the beginning, but once
ithe ‘ice is broken, they will be sparkling with vivacity.

Month of Thula (Oct. 20 10 Nov. 19 approx.) :
The life of these people will, for ithe most part, have
to be lived travelling. Further, in the course of their
work, they may have to do things which do not conform
to the accepted notions of propriety or picty. It surely
sounds absurd to say at this time that they will be
attracted by alchemy; but the old writers say as
much as that. Probably it denotes some of its modern
counterparts. A strong Sun however denotes
courage.
Month of Vrischik (Nov. 20 to Dec. 19 approx.) }
Rashness with a capital R will describe the mentality
of.these people. They are never in the habit of, not
even out of mistake, reflecting on the consequence of
a contemplated action. They will be adepts in ‘the
use of weapons. They will earn money in not very
proper ae and, sure as anything, such ill-gotten
money will not be useful to their own needs.
Mouth of Dhanu (Dec. 20 to Jan. 19 approx.) :
These are the great people whom even yogis
venerate. That mcans people of this month will he of
excellent character and education. Financially they
will be well off. They will have an abiding interest
in medicine and sculpture. If the Sun be strong
they will become successful busincssmen.
Month of Makar (Jan. 20 to Feb. tg approx.) :
Without any redeeming features in the horoscope,
one must say that these people will always do things
not eprraved by their social laws, that is, beneath
their dignity. More often than not, they will be
little educated. If they Happon to be businessmen, their
business will not be conducted on honourable lines.

24 EVERYDAY ASTROLOGY
The Leo born is a stalwart in the full sense of the
word. He has an imposing stature, is fond of sports
and recreations, and is generous of heart. He is
forgiving by nature. He is devoted to his parents.
but has very few issues. He is jealous of his fame
and unlikely to fall a viclim to flattery. He will in
some way be associated with kings or the govern-
ment. He is a potential spcculator or punter.
The Virgo born is a good linguist and has a
scientific turn of mind. He is for learning anything
and everything if only out of curiosity, Yet he is
shy as a maiden and timid as a lamb. Fond of
seer abe he has a good taste for all things elegant,
is fertility results in too many girls and too few
boys. He has to guard himself against digestive
troubles,
The Libya born is famous for his judgment;
he weighs both sides of a question thoroughly before
coming to a decision. He is an expert trader. He
is a lover of art and female socicty, Often he has
two names. He covets the property of others but
never fails to help his dependants. Usually popular,
he makes a good business partner,
The Scorpio born is notorious for his many
outstanding characteristics. It is the sign of dicta-
tors. His thoroughness is heartless, his onorgy appa~-
‘tently inexhaustible. He has an immense appotite
for sex and treats his partner as a beast. As a
child, he is extremely mischievous. He has a repu-
tation for secret crimes. He is likewise capable of ,
great heights of nobility and sacrifice, ;
The Sagittarius born is very alert, intuitive and
burrows to the point easily. He is free, generous and
reliable. A lover of art and poetry, he has creative ;
ability. Often he is short-sighted or hunch-backed. #
“He is, however, straightforward in his dealings and j
‘has a high sense of justice.

The Capricornus born is a type by himself. He is
ascetic in his ways. He has a singloncss of purpose
that is commendable. No amount of sacrifice to that
end is too dear for him. He is unoriginal but plodding
and persevering. He protects his family like the hen.
While he cannot be intimidated by force, he melts
like wax in the warmth of friendship and goodness.
The Aquarius born is a humanitarian with a
healthy outlook on life and its problems. He is
interested in all progressive things. He is kind, is
fond of Icarning and generally inspires noble thoughts.
The Pisces bon is not an impressive figure. He
is unoslentatious and even shy. Very often he is a
mystic or spititualist. He is cqually capable of be-
coming an astute businessman. ‘Wo loves the warmth
of the domestic hearth and generally proves successful
in transactions dealing with liquids or spirits.

The year, date and time of birth, and the latitude
and longitude of the place of birth are all the necessary
data for casting the horoscope either by the Indian
or the Western Method.
THE TepeMERIS \
In view, however, of the fact that there are in-
numerable panchangs or ephemerides in India differing
from province to province, both in terminology and
detail 1t has been thought desirable to stick {o the
Western method so far as Lhe mathematical portion of
the horoscope is concerned and convert the horoscope so
cast to the Indian system by subtracting the avanamsa
of the year of birth from the longitudes of the houses
and planets, This method is absolutely reliable and
does not give room to confusion. All that one has
to do is to find out the corresponding English date,
in the event of the date of birth being recorded
in terms of the Indian calendar, and work oul as
described in the pages that follow.
The most importanl requisites for computing a
horoscope according to the Westorn melhod are (z)'
Raphacl's Ephemeris for the year of birth which
corresponds to the Indian panchang and (2) Raphael's
Tables of Houses for Northern Latitudes, Though
there are several ephemerides, Raphael’s is the most
widely used and highly accurate.
“An ephemeris is an account of the Geocentric
places of the planets, and contains their Longitudes,
Latitudes and Declinations,” wriles Raphael, Describ«
ing his own ephemeris, he writes: ‘At the top of my
ephemeris, you will find the latitude and declination
of, V, i, b, 2, &, 2 and &, also the Moon’s nade,
and the ‘Mutual Aspects’....‘The

As we all know éhithis have their separate use in

branch when we say that some /hithis are good and
others bad, we mean that the relative positions of the
Sun and Moon on that day favour the [fulfilment of
given acts or destroy them, Whatever the nature of
the result, it becomes clear that particular elongations
of the Moon have a say in the affairs of men and things.
In other words ¢hithis are functional arcs in astrology.
In view of the very close relations between the natal
and electional arms of astrology, at any rate in basic
principles, it is extraordinary that so little is known of
its use in the judgment of horoscopes by the Indian
system,
Tt is admitted on all hands that astrology in its
fundamental aspects has been a common heritage to
all ancient civilizations. There are evidences galore
of interchange of knowledge of the occult sciences.
It is reasonable to presume therefore that knowledge
so gained had been improved upon by particular people
according to their particular genius. With this promise,
I may say, that, proof of the greater usc of this func-

natal branch from ancient days is available in the
Western system of astrology. Perhaps orientated

not thereby commenting upon the genins of one

According to the Indian system, these aspects
apply to the whole house, Further, these aspecis
are neither good nor bad by themselves; they depend
upon the planets in relation to one another and to
the horoscope.
ASPECTS : WESTERN SYSTEM

aspect all other planets, but certain well-defined aspects
alone are of account. And those aspects by themselves
are either good or bad as tabulated below :—

measurement is taken north or south of the
celestial equator as against the lateral measurement
which we call Longitude. If we suppose two planets
to be equidistant on either side of the celestial equator,
we say they aie situated in the same degree of declina-
tion, Irrespective of their longitudes, they attract each
other or aspect each other. It is this aspect that we
call Paiallel aspect represented by the symbol P.
Its effect is similar to the conjunction o&%.
SPECULUM
From the foregoing descriptions, it would be clear
that a horoscope is incomplete without a table of as-
pects called the Speculwm formed by the different
planets in the horoscope. Now the speculum is easily
computed in the following manner. All that.one has
to do is to take the planets one by one and count how
many degrees each is apart from the others,
anti-clockwise. If those distances correspond to any
of the degrees of the aspects enumerated above, those
aspects are said to be formed,
OrBs
Of course the difference in longitudes of planets
will not always be 30°, 45°, 60° or 90° exactly.
They may be a few degrees more or less, Now in
measuring aspects, we usually allow a margin of §8°
on both sides, This margin we call the Ord.
An aspect is said to be applying when a planet is
going to form an aspect with another, and separating
when an aspect has been formed and the planets are
going their own ways. The applying aspect is
more effective than the separating aspect.

speculum as follows :—Take the Sun first, Its lon-

MANDI IN THE 12 BHAVAS
M., in the rst House: Cruel, deceitful, mannerless,
arrogant, defective eye; sickly; immoral; not learned
in the Vedas and Shastras; dull-witted.
M, im the and House: Inelegant in speech;
quarrelsome; lives in forcign soil; devoid of wealth
and education; unable 10 understand intricate or
subtle points; unreliable; sensual.
M, in 3rd House: Inimical to brothers and
sisters; separation from relatives; arrogant; loudly
angry; shows great fervour in making money.
M. in 4th House: Devoid of wealth, education,
relatives, vehicles, home and comfort ; wanderer,
- M. im 5th House: Wavering mind; bad mental-
ity; bad character; small number of children; short-
lived.
M. in 6th House: Courageous; blessed with
excellent sons; déstructive of enemies; scientific turn
of mind.
M. in 7th House: Quarrelsome; detested by the
wiblic; ungrateful; dull-witted; many wives, or undesir-
ble wife.
M, in 8th House; Defective eye; defective face;

M, in oth House: Destructive of elders and
father; doing unholy acts, change of religion or caste,

THE SUB-PLANET MANDI 75
M. in 12th House: Devoid of enjoyable things
of life: adept in whining; excessive expenditure;
spendthrift.
Manpr In COMBINATION WITIL OTIIER PLANETS
Sun and M. Fates father; Moon and M. inimical
to mother. Mars and M. Destructive of brother.
Mercury and M, Destructive of intellect. Jtpiter
and M, Speaks ill of Vedas and shastras; slandcrer.
Venus and M, Infatuated; bereft of comfort; associates
with women of low calibre. Saturn and M, Leper.
Rahu and M. Danger of poisoning. Ket and M,
Danger from fire.
There is one good point worth mentioning
about this sub-planet. If the lord of the house
occupied by Mandi be in Kendra or trikona with
reference to the lagna, it bestows upon the native
plenty of riches and fame,
Another point to which attention of the reader
is drawn is this, This same sub-planet is sometimes
called by the name Gulika,” But UTTARA KALAM-
RITA a famous treatise on astrology makes a dis-
tinction between the two, as being the two different
sons of Saturn. There is also a small difference in
their positions. What is described in this chapter
is exclusively Mandi, although it is very common to
find all great writers making little discrimination
between the two. So long as we know that a certain
entity has a certain effect on the life of men and we
know it, it is immaterial by what name it is called.
EXCEPTION
This sub-planet becomes practically powerless
when either the lord of the day of birth or lord of lagna
as very strongly placed in the horoseope.

Although the roth house is generally considered
as the house of occupation, yet the root of occupation.
lies with the xst house. Saturn in the roth house
denotes rise in the latter half of native’s life; Mars
for rise through one’s own energy; Jupiter indicates
occupation in connecton with law or officialdom;
Uranus in the roth house indicates rise by revolution
. machines, electricity, invention, etc,
Successful businessmen need strong 2nd house
and well-placed, well-aspected 8. Strong connection
between @ and other planets is required for becoming
successful artists, Strong J’ or in a horoscope in-
dicates an engineer or technician, while strong 9 in-
dicates a politician.
A bad Mercury-Neptune combination is indicative
of the criminal; Mars in bad aspect with Saturn or
Neptune points to the murder suspect; if the 3th
house is also involved, murder by a sexual cause is
indicated.

Bhava lords occupying kendra or thrikona posi-

uchcha, own or friendly positions will strengthen the

‘“All kinds of prosperity should be predicted for
those bhavas whose trines and angles are occupied by
benefics and not occupied or aspected by malefics, nor
containing the lords of 6th, 8th and rath houses. A
reverse position will mean the opposite result, If
mixed, mixed results will follow.
Complete destiuction of bhava should be predicted
when the Sun occupies the 8th from it, lord of bhava
be combust, and no benefic lord of the 8th keeps
company.
Lords of bhavas bracketed with 8th house lord
indicate the destruction of the bhavas.
If the lord of a bhava occupies 6th, 8th or rath
house position or be neecha or in enemy’s house, then
the planet occupying the dhava, however good, is
incapable of lifting it Irom the morass.
A similar disability in the navamsa chart, too,
will indicate the same resull and vice-versa,
Although ill-placed in the lagna hundali, if lords
of bhavas occupy uchcha, own or friendly houses in the
navamsa chart, or be aspecled by benefics in the
navamsa chart, those bhavas are productive of good
result.
It will become evident from the last two rules
how important is the navamsa chart. 1 may totally
change the face of a horoscope. Hence it is necessary
to erect the correct navamsa kundali int each case and
predictions should not be given without reference
to it,

» very important consideration in the evaluation
of thée-stfength of bhavas is this. Syppose a bhava
lord is strong by position, say in a friend’s house,
whether in the lagna kundali or the navamsa kundalt.
Then if that friend happens to be weak by neecha or
similar disability, then the whole bottom is knocked
out of your contention that the original bhava is
strong, It follows that when the dispositois are
strong by positions like wchcha, friend’s or own places,
then the original bhavas become strong,
A bhava is said to be strong when friends of its
lord, his wehcha lord, that planet to which that bhava
is uchcha, occupy 1th, 2nd, or 3rd places. But
these planets should not be neecha, combust, or be
enemies to the houses, E
The strength of a bhava is proportionate to its
navamsa.
Predominance of malefic influences on bhavas
will destroy them.
The destruction of a bhava will also take place
during the pendency of the dasa or bhukti of the
planet which happens to be the lord of the and or
4th from that bhava, or posited there,
Here are some special poinis 10 be remembered
in this connection ; a good aspect of the lord of the
lagna to a particular bhava will ensure its success.
But if a malefic planet happens to be the lord of
bhava and aspects the same, then success is doubtful.
One must predict the nature of a house indication
from the nature of the influence that house receives,
Suppose we are considering the first house: an
aspect to this house from the lord of the 6th house
will cauge trouble through cnemies; aspect of 8th
houge lord will cause danger to life; aspect of rath
house lord will cause penury.

92 EVERYDAY ASTROLOGY
Affliction of wife is indicated if—
P
(x) Sun occupies the seventh hotise*in the
Rasi kundalt and the house of Mars in the
Navamsa kundali.
(2) Lords of second, seventh houses or
Venus in the sixth, eighth or twelfth house and/
or also otherwise afflicted,
(3) Venus hemmed in between two malefics
or malefics situated in the second, fourth or eighth
house from that of Venus.
The number of wives a man will marry is deter-
mined, inter alia, by the number of planets in the
seventh house, the malefics denoting death.
Venus or lord of seventh house occupying even
navamsas indicate more than one wife.
If the lord of the seventh house along with anyone
of Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus and Mars occupies the
sixth, eighth or the twelfth house, the native will
not enjoy married life in full measure.
The dagna of the girl whom a man will marry will
be one of these:
(x) Either the fifth or ninth, from the house
occupied by the lord of that man’s lagna or his
seventh house,
(2) The houses of exaltation of the lords of
the first or the seventh house in the man’s horos-
cope,
The direction of the locality in which the girl is
born is determined as follows :
Of the lord of the seventh house, the accu-
pant of the seventh house and Venus ascertain
which is the most powerful. The direction de-
noted by the housé owned by that planet will be
the required direction.

It is very common amongst Hindus, almost
compulsory, to consult the astrologer about a proposed
marriage alliance between a boy and a girl ta see
whether their horoscopes “agree.” The rules of
finding it are tenfold, but it is enough to know the
most important among them,
It is noteworthy that our ancients held that the
best. form of agreement between two parties is the
agreemerit of minds, 7.¢,, where there is mutual love,
Count the number of nakshairas from the girl’s to
that of the boy. Divide it by 9. If the remainder
is 4, 6 or 9, that will denote the best form of agreement,
i.e. it will assure a long married life to the couple,
x, 2, and 8 will be tolerable. The remainders are
unfavourable.

Again, if the lord of the 4th occupies fixed signs,
the person will perform his important functions in his
parental home. If in moveable signs, he will most
probably be doing them in placos other than that
of his nativity.
Fremate Horoscorres
All that have been told in the foregoing pages
apply mostly to male horoscopes ; with a slight adjust-
ment they can be made to apply to female horoscopes.
also. Specially, the eighth house in a female horoscope
denotes mangalya or lifofe th e hushand ; the ninth,
/ehildrén; seventh, her beauty, her husband; fourth,
her sexual life and chastity. It goes without saying
that these houses should as far as possible be un-
afflicted.
Enp or May
The problem of correct longevity or time of death
defies accurate solution even at the hands of seasoned
astrologers. Innumerable ways have been recom-
. mended by a succession of writers ancient and modern,
no two of which agrce in result, Perhaps it is a pur-
poselul mystery.
But it does not mean either that the science of
astrology is defective or that we cannot reach any~
where near correct solution. We certainly can reach
a very neat mark, One reason, however, why we
miss the bull’s eye is that we hardly get the time of
birth, correct to the degree which is required for
purposes of this kind.
r
The main significators for longevity, as we have
Icarnt, are: (1) the cighth house, (2) third House,
being the eighth from the latter, (3) lords of the above,
(4) all the three above significators with reference to
the Moon, (3) Saturn, being ayush karaka and (6) all
the first three significators with reference to Saturn.
Longevity is directly proportional to the strength of

long life. Ages below thirty, above thirty and below
sixty and over-sixty will answer the above categories,
The odds should be further reduced by the fol-
lowing process. Since 8th and 3rd houses have
been said to be the houses of longevity, the rath from
them, namely, 7th and 2nd houses will constitute the
houses of death. It has been observed that of the
two, 2nd is the more powerful. Technically they are
called maraka or death-dealing houses. JIpso facto
the lords thereof are potent killers.* But even more
powerful, it has been found, are the planets occupying
the 2nd and 7th houses. Most powerful are those pla-
nets that are closeled with the Jast two significators,
Death will, therefore, in the first instance, take place
during the pendency of the dasa or bhukti of the planets
belonging to the last category. The powers of other
significators will be in the descending order, In other
words thé occupants of the and and 7th houses will
come next, lords of the above two houses later, ete,
Alternatives arc mentioned because of possible ex-
tenuating circumstances like particular afflictions
not being able to operate during suspect periods,
or may be, particular malefactions may become
annulled due to aspects from the lord of the horoscope
or benefics, etc.
Last come in the above hierarchy, planets which
receive the aspects of the malefactors,

104. EVERYDAY ASTROLOGY
Again, we keep the original houses stationary
and progress the planets at the same rates and see
what aspects they throw on the M.C., and Ascendant,
This is also interpreted and taken note of,
We next proceed to the second step, namely,
Secondary Direction. The basis in this method is
this: the actual positions of the planets on the birth
map each day following birth indicate the character-
istics of each year of the following birth. Thus if
the actual positions of the planets on the tenth day are
marked in the new map (the time however is kept the
same), this new chart will represent the happenings
for the tenth year of life,
It is clear that the majority of planets will not
have moved far cnough in such a short time as ten
days. In any case we take all into account. Then
we must collect all the aspects formed in the interval
vf twenty-four hours from the time of birth on the
equired day. Suppose tenth is the date of birth and
ve want the reading for the twelfth year of life ; we
hen collect all aspects formed on the twenty-first of
that month (of course of the same year) from the time
of birth till the same hour on the next day.
This process of collecting the aspects is very
much simplified if we look up the Complete Aspectarian
given by Raphael’s Ephemeros each year where the
actual hour and minute of the formation of all those
aspects are also given. Only the time of birth which
we are spcaking of here must be the G.M.T. corres~-
Ponding to the time of birth in places other than.
Teenwich,
These aspects with their times must be copied
down separately. It is interesting 1o note that
Raphael's Ephemeris gives even the nature of those
aspects as either very good (G), good (g), very bad (B),
bad (b), Doubtful (D), etc. ;

DIRECTIONS r05
Now what you have to do is to equate this interval
of twenty-four hours into twelve months and identify
the times of the formation of those aspects with the
particular dates corresponding to the life of the native,
The rate of conversion is this :
rt hour=15 days.
We now pass on to the next method Transists.
Suppose we have found by means of the above two.
methods that at a certain date an event is to happen.
Then in order to make sure that it is coming, we use
the method of Transits. Take Raphael's E-phemeris
for the year in which the event is prognosticated.
Turn to the actual month and date. See if on that
date any major combination of planets takes place
which may have a bearing on the horoscope under
examination. If there is corroboration, say that the
event will take place. Sometimes we might find in
Transit, a contrary indication. Then we have to take
it that the event will not take place. It is noteworthy
that the directions by themselves are not quite reliable
but that they require corroboration from Transits.
The effects of directions should be predicted
according to the nature of the planets with particular
reference to the horoscopes. For a detailed prognosis
by directions, I would recommend the reader to refer
to Alan Leo’s Progressed Horoscope.

CHAPTER 18
DASAS : THEIR MECHANISM
In Indian astrology events ate timed by (x) planetary
periods called Dasas and (2) Transits called Gocharas,
We shall deal with the first in this chapter.
According to the Dasa sysiem, a man’s life is
divided into periods, sub-periods and minor sub-
periods which are characterised by the different planets.
In Dasas there are two main varicties, vzz,, the
Ashottart and Vinshottari dasas, For ou part, we
shall study the latter alone as it has been found to
give larger percentage of correct. results,
In Vinshottart, the basis is that a man’s life lasts
for 120 years and this period is divided among planets
as follows: Sun 6 yrs.; Moon ro yrs.; Mars 7 yrs. ;
Rahu 18 yrs.; Saturn r9 yrs,; Mercury 17 yrs.; Ketu
years and Venus 20 years. These are the major
periods and they follow this fixed order,
In effect the passage of the 3 along its next 120
degrees (from birth) or a third of the full zodiac, is
taken as reflecting the life of a person*. This concep-
tion bears a close resemblance to Primary Directions,
although the mechanism of interpretation is a little
different.
Each major period is again sub-divided into nine
sub-periods called Bhuktis which are proportionate
to the number of years assigned to each in the major
period, and this sub-division also follows the same
fixed order, The first sub-period will always belong
to the same planet that rules over the major period,
Each sub-period is again divided into minor sub-~
periods called Antavas and Sukshmas. A separate table
giving the exact measure of these divisions is given
at the end of this chapter. For an exhaustive treat-
ment of the rationale of the Dasas the reader is
referred to that excellent book “Directional Astrology
of the Hindus,” by Dr. Rele.

Dasas : THEIR MECHANISM XIE
So all that we have to do is to calculate the longi-
tude of the Moon from the time of birth from Raphael's
Ephemeris and subtract from it the ayanamsa of the
year of birth. This will give us the exact position of
the Moon according 10 the Indian system. By refer-
ring to the above table, we can immediately find what
the opening dasa is. What remains for us is to find
how much of the opening dasa is outstanding at the
time of birth.
It has already been shown that the measure of a
nakshatva is 13° 20’, So, the total amount of the
years of the opening dasa must be equated io this
13° 20’ and that portion of the years which is propor-
tionate 10 the degrees yet to be traversed by the Moon
in order to complete that vakshatva must be found. This
will be the outstanding years of the opening dasa. The
other dasas will follow afterwards in the fixed order,
An illustration will simplify the matter. In our
first example, the longitude of the Moon after taking
away the ayanamsa is 11° 44' 34" in Sagittarius or
a5x° 44’ 34” from the First Point of Aries.
Referring to the Table of Nakshatvas (Chap. 6)
we find that the Moon has travelled r1° 44’ 34” in
Moola nakshatva, Again referring this to the Table
of Dasa Allotments we find that for Moola, the opening
dasa is that of Ketu and its duration is 7 years. Now

Similarly in the major period of a harmful planet,
the sub-periods of good planets which are un-influenced
by the ruling planet, are hardly productive of good
results, Those that are influcnced give mixed results.
The highly beneficial effects of a planet that gives
vaja yoga manifest themselves in the sub-period of
the maraka (dceath-dealing) planet during ihe major
period of the former. The good results go on increas-
ing in the sub-periods of ‘harmful plancts during the
same major period,
The major periods of those planets which are the
lords of the third, fifth or the seventh nakshatras from
the janma nakshatra are also evil.
In general, the good effects of favourable planets
begin to take shape when the Sun or Jupiter usher
their sub-periods in the major period of the former.

RECTIFICATION OF HOROSCOPES 139
WESTERN SYSTEM
If, however, the horoscope is cast according to
the Western system in Case (it) the method is entirely
inalogous to the one detailed above.
In cases of doubtful horoscopes, however, two
mportant methods are handled of which we shall
lescribe only one as the other involves higher mathe-
natics.
We have stated that the M.C. in a horoscope
noves forward at the rate of 1° which we took to signify
ye year of life and that the positions of planets on each
lay following birth indicated the events of each year
‘ollowing birth, We now have just to reverse the
srocess for purposes of rectification.
Let us suppose that in the horoscope of Hitler the
rirth time is uncertain. Then we take the major events
of his life one by one. We know that he lost his father .
ub r2 years of age. So, the progressed M.C. must
1ave been in conjunction with the place of Saturn at
chat time, In other words the true M.C. must be
tbout 12° behind Saturn’s position. We thus arrive
it the true M.C. by subtracting 12° from the longitude
{ Saturn, Once the M.C. is fixed, the other houses are
asily fixed,

NATIONAL AND FINANCIAL ASTROLOGY I5r
BULLION
It is pretty easy to find out the price movements
of the king metals—gold and silver. The kavakas for
them (prices) are respectively Sun and Mercury. AIL
that you have to do is to watch the movements of
these two planets in relation to other planets by
referring to their longitudes,
Here is a practical method. Take hold of Ra-
phael’s Ephemerts. Towards the end there is a section
called Complete Aspectarian. In that section the
aspects formed between all planets each day and their
lime in G.M.T, are given. You must take the parti-
cular day and pick out the aspects in which the Sun
(for gold) and Mercury (for silver) are involved, Note
them down separately along with the time and the
mark G, g, B, b, etc. Since these times are G.M.T.
you must add hrs. 5.30 to each, which will give I.S,T.
G¥means, as you may know, very good ; g tolerably
good. ; B very bad and b rather bad etc. From these
indications you can understand that the price structure
will move up or come down,
In so calculating, the position of Sun or Moon
should be borne in mind, whether it is occupying its
own, tuchcha or friend’s house which will make an
appreciable difference in the assessment.
Corton
As already mentioned, Mercury is the haraka
for cotton production and Venus cotton price struc-
ture. As explained in the case of bullion, you must
pick out those aspects that contain Venus and Mercury,
their time converted to IST and they should be inter-
reted in the samc manner. Due consideration should
e given to house positions of Venus and Mercury,
This is a practical way of predicting speculative com-
modifies.

NOTABLE NATIVITIES 165
The presence of Rahu in the first house indicates
the birth-pangs of the Dominion of India of which
we are all too familiar, Uranus and Mandi in and
house denote partition of land and resources; also
precarious food position. Six powerful plancts in
the third house, the house of brothers, indicate the
brotherhood of nations in which India finds herself
today, The third house is the place for courage and
its lord Mgon is strong not only by lagna but by amsa
also, being vargottaa, India’s courage, therefore, is
beyond doubt.’ The fourth house in financial astro-
logy connotes the real foundation of business. There
is nothing much to be said,except that its lord is in
good company and that he obtains Jupiter’s amsa,
lifth house is the house of speculation and it is occu-
picd by the chaos-breeding planet Neptune and. is
aspected by Mars, This is a dangerous portent, But
Saturn also aspects the house which will have a steady-
ing effect, Jupiter in the 6th house ensures faithful
servants of the state, The 7th house denotes the
relation between the state and the people. The
presence of Ketu will not permit altogether smooth
sailing, The 8th denotes credit position, loans, etc.
This house is aspected by Mars and Uranus which
show a highly inflationary tendency, gth house
indicates long-term planning and legal matters, The
Jord of the house aspects it. A number of other
planets aspect it. We may take it therefore that
there will be plenty of them. Tenth represents
reputation, prestige in international circles. The 6th
from it contains six planets of which its lord is one.
There will be no lack of pitfalls and enemics to this
aspect, But Saturn will hold them in check. Jupiter
is turned malefic duc to house position and hence its
aspect to the house should be taken on the debit side.
Presence of Rahu in the 4th from this house indicates
it is not a bed of roses. 11th denotes policies, hold on
the people and the quality of goods it delivers. Nep-
